events.title: Big Ben Begins Keeping Time
events.description: The Great Clock of the Palace of Westminster in London, whose bell is popularly known as Big Ben, started operating and keeping time for the first time.
events.significance: Big Ben became one of the most recognizable symbols of London and the United Kingdom, and a landmark of Victorian engineering and precision timekeeping.

events.title: Johnstown Flood
events.description: The failure of the South Fork Dam in Pennsylvania after heavy rains sent a wall of water into Johnstown, killing more than 2,200 people.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest disasters in U.S. history up to that time, prompted the American Red Cross's first major peacetime relief effort led by Clara Barton, and influenced American liability law.

events.title: Union of South Africa Established
events.description: The Union of South Africa was formed as a self-governing dominion of the British Empire, merging the Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River Colony.
events.significance: The Union unified the four colonies under one government dominated by the white minority, laying the foundation for the political structures that later led to apartheid.

events.title: Battle of Jutland Begins
events.description: The British Royal Navy's Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet clashed in the North Sea off Denmark's Jutland coast, in the largest naval battle of World War I and one of the biggest battleship engagements in history.
events.significance: Though Germany inflicted heavier losses, Britain retained control of the North Sea and its blockade, and the German fleet largely stayed in port for the rest of the war.

events.title: Ancash Earthquake in Peru
events.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake off the coast of Peru triggered a massive avalanche from Huascarán that buried the town of Yungay and parts of Ranrahirca.
events.significance: With roughly 70,000 deaths, it was the deadliest earthquake in Peruvian history and one of the worst natural disasters in the Western Hemisphere, shaping later disaster preparedness in the Andes.
